subject_session: 8 sessions/8 mice (sub-AK190207A/C, AK190208, AK190502A/B, AK190506, AK210825B, HK190525); primary sub-HK190525_ses-tones1

headline_stat.name: fraction of units with significant frequency tuning

justification.dataset: A pure-tone A1 dataset is per the rubric not sufficient for true STRFs (which need spectrotemporally rich stimuli), so the spectrotemporal phenomenon cannot be cleanly isolated, though the spectral/frequency-tuning dimension is genuinely present and the agent used the best available auditory dataset.
justification.handling: Real streamed data from 8 sessions, explicit 'good'-quality unit filtering, correct LED-off control-trial exclusion, and correct trial alignment confirmed by stimulus-locked bursts in the raster.
justification.analysis: Kruskal-Wallis per-unit tuning plus a population binomial-vs-chance test is valid and appropriately handles multiple comparisons, though ~9 trials/frequency leaves the per-unit tests underpowered (only 11% tuned in A1).
justification.correctness: Reported values (11.3%, p=3.3e-5, median 40 ms) reproduce from the committed code, are internally consistent with the figures, and are physically possible.
justification.figures: Figures are well-labeled with units and sample sizes and the population-average panel clearly shows the BF-aligned excitatory center, but the example STRF panels are noisier than the 'sharp/confined-to-a-narrow-band' text implies.
justification.honesty: The population finding is real and supported, but the write-up describes visibly noisy example units as 'clean, sharply tuned, confined to a narrow band,' states no limitations about the marginal per-unit significance or the pure-tone-vs-true-STRF substitution — mild overstatement, not fabrication.
justification.verdict: Core population analysis is sound and reproducible, but I would require toning down the overstated example descriptions, adding limitations, and acknowledging that pure tones do not yield a true STRF before accepting.
